apiDocs.title: API Reference
apiDocs.subtitle: Every HTTP endpoint MonitorFlare exposes: unauthenticated status data, the API-key-gated full data endpoints, the inbound webhook, and an index of admin routes.
apiDocs.baseUrlHint: All samples below use it as the prefix. /api/… and the same path without /api are equivalent — the entrypoint rewrites the prefix, so both spellings work.
apiDocs.pathVarHint: :id / :token in the path are placeholders — the URL above shows sample values. It is a path parameter; don't pass it again as a query parameter.
apiDocs.overviewP1: Every endpoint returns JSON (except /api/feed.xml, which is RSS XML). On failure the body is always {'{'} "error": "…" {'}'} with a matching HTTP status code.
apiDocs.overviewL1: Public endpoints need no credentials, but they still respect site visibility: on a private site, status endpoints require a token exchanged from the access password, or admin credentials.
apiDocs.overviewL2: /api/v1 is the API-key-gated data layer, covering logs, incidents, uptime breakdowns and a full-site export.
apiDocs.overviewL3: Write and admin operations require a signed-in admin session or an API key.
apiDocs.authIntro: Pass the credential as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. Keys are created under “API Keys” in the admin panel.
apiDocs.authKeyDesc: Starts with ut_ and is shown in full only once at creation time. Grants /api/v1/* and every admin route; keys are not scoped read/write — delete one to revoke it.
apiDocs.authSessionDesc: Short-lived session issued after signing in. Carries full admin rights, handy for quick browser-side debugging.
apiDocs.authStatusDesc: Required for public endpoints when the site is private. Exchange the access password via POST /api/status/login.
apiDocs.authCfDesc: Sent through the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header; no extra login needed once Zero Trust is enabled.
apiDocs.publicDesc: Visitor-facing status data that needs no credentials — ideal for status pages, dashboards and third-party integrations. Responses are cached for a few dozen seconds, so polling frequently is safe.
apiDocs.epStatus: First-screen snapshot of the status page: current state, 7/30-day uptime and latency for every monitor, plus active incidents.
apiDocs.epStatusNote: On a private site this endpoint needs a status page access token or admin credentials, otherwise it returns 401.
apiDocs.epMonitorsPublic: Monitor list: by default only display fields (including certificate and domain expiry) — no alerting rules or other config. Add ?detail=1 to also get latency, uptime and 90 days of daily stats.
apiDocs.epMonitorsPublicNote: ?scope=public switches to the public view (no credentials needed). Without an id it returns every monitor. Pass ?id=1 or ?ids=1,2,3 to fetch only specific ones — filtering happens server-side, so you don't have to pull the full list and filter it yourself. A single monitor's logs, latency series and incidents come from this same path with ?view=detail&id=.
apiDocs.pScope: public switches to the public view (what the status page reads: no credentials, trimmed fields). Omit it for the admin view, which needs a token. Any other value returns 400.
apiDocs.pView: detail returns a single monitor object (exactly one id required); omit it for the list shape.
apiDocs.pMonitorId: Return only this monitor; must be a positive integer. Omit it to get all of them.
apiDocs.pMonitorIds: Comma-separated monitor IDs (50 at most). Can be combined with id — results are merged and de-duplicated.
apiDocs.pDetail: Set it to 1 to add latency, uptime and 90 days of daily stats; the response becomes {'{'} monitors: [...] {'}'}. Omit it for the slim array.
apiDocs.epMonitorDetail: Complete detail for one monitor: base info, multi-window uptime, latency series, recent logs and related incidents.
apiDocs.epMonitorDetailNote: range controls the window for latency_series and logs; limit only caps the number of logs. The legacy paths /api/monitors/public/detail and /api/monitors/public/:id are rewritten to this one and still work.
apiDocs.epIncidentsActive: Currently active incidents and scheduled maintenance (status = active only).
apiDocs.epIncidentsActiveNote: Historical (including resolved) incidents require auth — use /api/incidents?status=all or /api/v1/incidents.
apiDocs.epFeed: RSS 2.0 feed of the 20 most recent incidents, ready for any RSS reader or Slack.
apiDocs.epFeedNote: On a private site the access password check still applies.
apiDocs.epSubscribe: Subscribe to status change emails. A confirmation / unsubscribe email is sent on success.
apiDocs.epUnsubscribeNote: token comes from the unsubscribe link in the confirmation email.
apiDocs.v1Desc: The API-key-gated data layer covering logs, incidents, uptime and full-site export. Built for Grafana, custom reporting or archival.
apiDocs.epV1Monitors: Full configuration and current state of every monitor (no uptime aggregates).
apiDocs.epV1MonitorsNote: Sensitive values are masked automatically — for example Authorization / Cookie entries inside request_headers.
apiDocs.epV1Logs: Paginated probe logs. The workhorse endpoint for custom charts and incident forensics.
apiDocs.epV1LogsNote: since / until filter on both created_at and log id; stick to YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss.
apiDocs.epV1Incidents: All incidents in reverse chronological order, including resolved and cancelled ones.
apiDocs.epV1Uptime: Daily uptime and average latency aggregates, plus a per-monitor summary for the whole window.
apiDocs.epV1UptimeNote: daily is per-monitor per-day detail, summary covers the entire window — use either one on its own.
apiDocs.epV1Export: Full-site data snapshot for backup or migration.
apiDocs.epV1ExportNote: limit caps the number of logs; secret-like settings are filtered out and never leak into the export.
apiDocs.webhookDesc: Let external systems (monitors, CI, alerting platforms) push events onto your status page. The URL is generated under Settings → Inbound Webhook.
apiDocs.epWebhook: Push an event; it is created as an active incident and broadcast to every subscriber immediately.
apiDocs.epWebhookNote: The token is the credential — treat it like a password. Regenerate it in the admin panel to invalidate the old one.
apiDocs.pId: Monitor ID (required, exactly one). Fetch it first from /api/monitors?scope=public.
apiDocs.pUnsubToken: Unsubscribe token from the confirmation email.
apiDocs.pMonitorId: Filter by monitor ID. Omit it to return every monitor.
apiDocs.pUntil: End of the range (inclusive). Defaults to now.
apiDocs.pOffset: Offset, pair it with limit to page through results.
apiDocs.pWebhookToken: Inbound webhook token generated in the admin panel; it lives in the URL path.
apiDocs.adminIntro: These routes require an admin session or an API key and are meant for operations and automation. They are not public data and their fields evolve between versions — click through once in the admin panel and observe the real payload before writing a script against them.
apiDocs.adminHealth: Health check reporting database and site component readiness.
apiDocs.adminMonitors: Monitor list with every field, alert config included. One endpoint, several shapes via query params: bare for the plain list, ?include=stats to add multi-window uptime and latency, ?id=3&include=logs to add that monitor's recent logs.
apiDocs.adminMonitorAction: Run one action on the monitor named by ?id=: probe it now, or pause / resume it. check, pause and batch (bulk) are three values of this same POST — see the params table.
apiDocs.adminMonitorConfig: Update the configuration of the monitor named by ?id=.
apiDocs.adminMonitorDelete: Delete the monitor named by ?id= together with its history.
apiDocs.pAdminInclude: Comma-separated extras: logs adds recent checks per monitor, stats adds multi-window uptime and latency. Anything else returns 400. Omit it for the plain monitor list.
apiDocs.pAdminLimit: Log rows when include=logs is set: 1 – 500, default 50. Across monitors it pages the whole result set — not that many rows per monitor.
apiDocs.pAdminOffset: Pages alongside limit, default 0. Also applies only to the logs of include=logs.
apiDocs.pMonitorAction: check probes it right now; pause pauses or resumes — with no body it toggles the current state, pass body {'{'} paused: 0|1 {'}'} to set it; batch pauses / resumes / deletes / probes in bulk, with the target ids in the body. Omit action entirely to create a monitor. Any other value returns 400.
apiDocs.pReorderAction: reorder re-sorts monitors into the order of the ids in the body. It is the only value PUT accepts here; anything else returns 400.
apiDocs.pTargetId: Id of the target to act on. Member operations do not take a path — the target always comes from this param. Missing or not a positive integer returns 400.
apiDocs.pTemplateAction: duplicate copies it into a new version (named "(copy)"); default moves the default flag here — only one default exists, and channels without their own template fall back to it. Any other value returns 400.
apiDocs.pChannelAction: test sends one test notification rendered with the template version bound to that channel. Pass ?id= to probe a single channel, omit it to notify every enabled channel. Any other value returns 400.
apiDocs.adminMonitorsBatch: Pause / resume / delete / probe monitors in bulk, with the target ids in the body.
apiDocs.adminIncidentsAll: All incidents and maintenance records, resolved ones included.
apiDocs.adminIncidentsCreate: Create an incident or a maintenance notice.
apiDocs.adminIncidentsUpdate: Update the status and progress of the incident named by ?id=.
apiDocs.adminSettingsGet: Read site settings; password fields come back as placeholders.
apiDocs.adminChannelsUpdate: Update the channel named by ?id=, including enabling and disabling it.
apiDocs.adminChannelsTest: Send one test notification through the channel named by ?id=, to see what it would receive.
apiDocs.adminTestAlert: Send one test notification to every enabled channel.
apiDocs.adminTemplatesUpdate: Update the content of the template version named by ?id=.
apiDocs.adminTemplatesAction: Run one action on the template named by ?id=: copy it into a new version, or make it the default version.
apiDocs.adminTemplatesDelete: Delete the template version named by ?id=. The default version and the last remaining one cannot be deleted.
apiDocs.adminKeysList: List API keys — prefix and metadata only.
apiDocs.adminKeysCreate: Create an API key; the plaintext is returned only in this response.
apiDocs.adminKeysDelete: Delete the API key named by ?id=.
apiDocs.adminBackupExport: Export the whole site as a JSON backup.
apiDocs.adminBackupRestore: Restore the whole site from a backup file.
apiDocs.errorsIntro: On failure the body looks like {'{'} "error": "Unauthorized" {'}'}; the HTTP status code is the error category.
apiDocs.err400: Missing or invalid parameter — e.g. no title, or a malformed monitor id.
apiDocs.err401: No credential or an invalid one; private sites return status_page_locked when signed out.
apiDocs.err404: Target does not exist — e.g. /api/monitors?scope=public&view=detail&id=1 for an unknown monitor.
apiDocs.err500: Server-side failure; the error field carries the detail.
apiDocs.err503: Admin auth is not configured yet, or the site is not initialised.
apiDocs.limit1: /api/v1/logs caps at 5000 rows, /api/v1/incidents at 1000, and /api/v1/export at 5000 logs per call.
apiDocs.limit2: /api/status and /api/monitors?scope=public are served from an in-memory cache (~tens of seconds). Poll those instead of walking the logs repeatedly.
apiDocs.limit3: An API key's “last used” timestamp is written back at most once per hour, not on every call.
apiDocs.limit4: CORS is governed by ALLOWED_ORIGIN in the backend; add your frontend domain to the allowlist if direct browser calls are blocked.
